summary: Vol. 6 No. 1 (Jan. 7, 2022), 12 pages, bilingual English/Spanish Trenton weekly. Covers a fatal Christmas Day arson in Trenton, the funeral of a 17-year-old who died by suicide, a school-security funding bill, a Toys for Tots giveaway, 2021 Black celebrity obituaries, an editorial on the Minority Business Development Agency becoming permanent, a COVID health-disparity editorial, book reviews, and the announcement of the 2022 National Black Political Convention in Newark.

incidents.what: Fatal arson fire at 200 block of Rusling St. and Division St., Trenton, during Christmas; six adjacent houses and vehicles burned.
Mercer County prosecutor's office announced suspect Ronal Ordóñez Lima, 28, arrested and charged with murder in the Christmas Day Trenton arson.
Mercer CCYC toy giveaway to families with young children, with West Trenton Toys for Tots and US Marine Corps.
Funeral service for Christopher David, 17, held at Ledford Home, Trenton; mother says he died after struggling with depression and school bullying.
NJ Assembly Appropriations Committee introduced bill A-6258, allocating $5,150,531 for school security projects (panic alarms) statewide.
President Biden signed the Bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, making the Minority Business Development Agency permanent.
Newark Mayor Ras Baraka announced the 2022 National Black Political Convention, to be held April 28-May 1, 2022 at NJIT.
First National Black Political Convention (Gary Convention) held in Gary, Indiana, through March 12, 1972; adopted the Gary Declaration.
